activity.notes: After Constantine VI was overthrown in 797, Irene ruled the Byzantine Empire in her own right until her deposition in 802. This is the sole sovereign-reign phase and is therefore modeled as rules/reign rather than regency governance.

sources.title: Political Power and Christian Faith in Byzantium: The Case of Irene (Regent 780-90, Emperor 797-802)
sources.citation_text: Judith Herrin states that Irene ruled alone from 797 to 802, an unprecedented case in Byzantine history.

sources.title: Administrative Elites and Political Change
sources.citation_text: Cambridge scholarship identifies Irene as the reigning empress from 797 to 802 after earlier periods of co-regency with Constantine VI.

sources.title: The Empress Irene the Athenian
sources.citation_text: Steven Runciman describes Irene as the first woman in recorded European history to reign as a sovereign monarch and treats her reign as a period of major Byzantine political and ecclesiastical importance.
